coverage.main: Read all thirteen pages of arXiv 1901.08846v3 (29 May 2019), including references and appendices. Visually inspected pp. 6-8 for Table 1, experiment scopes and all eight Figure 3 heatmaps.
coverage.supplement: Retrieved the separately linked three-page PMLR supplement from the official proceedings page; read and visually inspected all pages. It contains proofs, JS-divergence and temperature-scaling analyses, and an ensemble-diversity histogram, overlapping arXiv Appendices A/B. Its Figure 1 corresponds to arXiv Figure 5, not an additional transfer experiment.
coverage.excluded_results: Figure 3 diagonals attack and evaluate the same member and are white-box; retain only off-diagonals as transfer. Tables 2-4 and Table 5 evaluate white-box ensemble robustness, not cross-member transfer. Figure 2 is feature visualization; Figure 4 is detection ROC/AUC, whose 1,000 normal plus 1,000 adversarial examples must not be assigned to Figure 3. The appendix histogram's 10,000-sample population is likewise not a transfer denominator. Table 1 is retained as clean-performance evidence, not transfer data.

f1.evidence: Table 1 reports CIFAR-10 clean errors separately for all three members in each Figure 3 training setting: baseline 8.30%, 8.52%, 8.67%; ADP(2,0.5) 9.34%, 9.34%, 9.92%. The same members act as sources and targets. This establishes separate clean reporting, not attack-cohort alignment.

f2.evidence: No explicit target-clean-correct denominator rule is stated for any of the eight transfer groups. The nominal 10,000 test examples and the separate detection experiment's 1,000 examples do not establish Figure 3 selection.

f3.evidence: No explicit successful-source restriction or retention of source failures is stated for the transfer heatmaps. Released full-test ensemble evaluation is not evidence of the member-transfer implementation.

f4.evidence: Heatmaps display fractions to two decimal places without exact transfer numerators or denominators. Dataset size is not an established heatmap denominator, and even assuming 10,000 would not uniquely reconstruct counts from this precision. No matching per-example records were located.

f5.evidence: All Figure 3 attacks have epsilon=0.05 on [0,1]-scaled pixels. Section 2.2 gives gradient-sign updates and clip(x,epsilon), but calls this a clipping function without explicitly specifying its norm or the PGD initialization neighborhood's norm. These are consistent with L-infinity attacks, but the attack name and the ensemble-only code do not by themselves establish the reported member-transfer norm under the frozen rule. White-box C&W/EAD/JSMA scopes are not the reason for this judgment.

f6.locator: Pinned public release README.md, test_cifar_iterative.py, utils.py and standard ADP checkpoint
f6.evidence: Code and a readable three-member ADP checkpoint are accessible. The inspected iterative evaluator attacks and scores the averaged ensemble rather than source/target member pairs; no Figure 3 runner or matching per-example outcomes was located. A member-level adapter and configuration/provenance verification remain necessary before declaring a sufficient original transfer configuration. Baseline availability is not imposed as a requirement for an ADP-only configuration.

artifact_checks.result: Verified official main-paper, supplementary-PDF and code links. Downloaded and inspected the complete three-page supplement; no additional transfer evaluation found.

Cloned public release and confirmed local/remote HEAD match. Read README, iterative CIFAR evaluator, utilities and ensemble wrapper; searched repository for transfer, target-accuracy calls, model evaluation and checkpoint loads. Iterative evaluation constructs three members, loads concatenated weights, attacks their averaged predictions and scores that same ensemble on x_test/y_test. It does not implement Figure 3 member-to-member evaluation. No original runtime was executed.

HEAD 200, 10,751,072 bytes. Downloaded and hashed checkpoint; read HDF5 structure without executing model code. Contains model_weights, optimizer_weights and serialized model/training configuration, with three 10-unit Dense outputs concatenated. Metadata says Keras 2.2.2/tensorflow, whereas README environment says Keras 2.2.4. This verifies readable model data, not matching Table 1 clean performance or Figure 3 checkpoint identity.
HEAD 200, advertised 10,754,184 bytes. Contents not downloaded or executed. This adversarially trained checkpoint is not substituted for the standard ADP member-transfer setting.

Legacy environment is Python 2.7.12, TensorFlow-GPU 1.9.0, Keras 2.2.4 and CleverHans 2.1.0. README requires a manual clipping patch for mean-subtracted inputs. The evaluator subtracts the training-set pixel mean and passes array-valued image-domain clip limits. Preserve both details when adapting; do not silently choose a different clipping path. Training commands are not the original weights. README download basenames and evaluator checkpoint paths also require explicit mapping.

bounds_checks.locator: Table 1, Section 4.4, Figure 3; released iterative evaluator
bounds_checks.reason: There are 24 off-diagonal untargeted accuracy cells and separately reported target-member clean errors. However, equality of the clean-test and attacked populations, absence of source-success selection, and exact checkpoint correspondence have not been established. Do not subtract Table 1 errors from 1 minus these cells yet. The ensemble evaluator cannot resolve the member-transfer population.

The 24 targeted off-diagonal cells measure specific-target-label success, not unconditional misclassification. Neither those values nor one minus those values can replace the required attacked error probability.

limitations: This is a non-blind evidence audit, not an independent recode or a validated replication.
No numerical bounds or recomputed PTR/CTR quantities are added. An accessible checkpoint is useful progress but not proof of the paper-to-code configuration mapping.
The positive separate-clean-reporting judgment must remain visible even though the more demanding population-aligned bounds check is unresolved.
